Subject: NYC Roundtable — lead export and follow-ups

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for partnering with us for the NYC roundtable. Attached is the lead export from onsite scans and badge swipes (nyc-roundtable-leads.csv). We included a source column that indicates whether the lead was generated via TechPartner co-hosting, our event platform, or direct signups.

- We flagged 12 as partner-sourced (TechPartner).

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Sophie Marlowe <sophie@techpartner.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: NYC Roundtable — lead export and follow-ups

Forwarding ACME's export — thank you for the quick turnaround. Two immediate asks for our post-show reconciliation:

1) Ben/Marissa — can you reconcile these 78 leads with our demo/conversion tracking? HubSpot shows 9 demo requests tied to the event but only 4 have source=roundtable. Looks like attribution rules may have overwritten partner attribution to last-touch.

2) Lauren — finance asked whether any credits/boomerang leads will need to be adjusted for the InnoBank opportunity (INN-4729).

Sophie — can you confirm which leads TechPartner considers co-sourced? ACME flagged 12, but some look like matchbacks from our CRM.

I attached a quick pivot I made (multi-touch-vs-first-touch-diff.xlsx) — it's rough but shows the discrepancy between first-touch (on-site) and HubSpot last-touch.

Goal: produce a final attribution table by EOD Monday so we can share with finance and the account team.

Thanks — Priyom
(attachments: multi-touch-vs-first-touch-diff.xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: NYC Roundtable — lead export and follow-ups

Priyom — quick notes after recon with the events export:

- I matched 72 / 78 rows to CRM records (6 were vendors/duplicates we suppressed).
- Of the 72, HubSpot currently attributes 47 as last-touch = "email nurture" or "organic site". Only 13 are marked first-touch=on-site.
- TechPartner-sourced flag: ACME's 12 map to 9 CRM records; 3 were anonymized scans.

Interpretation: our default last-touch rule (UTM > campaign activity > last engagement) is overwriting on-site attribution unless the visitor converts immediately after the event. For pipeline reporting we'd prefer a multi-touch weighted model; finance prefers a conservative first-touch credit.

Attached: brief reconciliation steps and the mapping I used. If we switch to first-touch for event-sourced pipeline, this will add ~ $186k in pipeline to INN-4729 (pending credit approval).

-Ben
(attachment: ben-roundtable-recon-notes.txt)

From: Sophie Marlowe <sophie@techpartner.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Events Ops <events@acmevents.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: NYC Roundtable — lead export and follow-ups

Thanks for the clarification — and congrats on a packed roundtable. A couple of clarifications from TechPartner side:

- Our co-sourced leads are any contact who explicitly selected "TechPartner" when registering or who scanned at the TechPartner table. We can provide our native export to match UIDs if that helps.
- We prefer multi-touch attribution for partner reporting, but are OK with a hybrid approach (first-touch credit for partner-sourced leads + weighted follow-ons).

I can share our export by EOD today (will include our reg IDs). If that lines up with ACME's 9/12 mapping, we can finalize who claims the lead.

Sophie
Senior Partnerships Manager | TechPartner
(sophie@techpartner.io)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NYC Roundtable — lead export and follow-ups

Team — finance note: do not finalize any pipeline credit or apply partner revenue recognition until we have:

1) Confirmed lead ownership (CRM match or partner UID)
2) A signed mutual action plan (MAP) or documented partner credit policy for these leads
3) A final attribution table that clearly lists source, touch history, and suggested credit percentage

Rebecca from InnoBank is looped for visibility. If the change Ben proposed (+$186k) is real, we need an approval chain before reflecting in forecasts.

Please deliver the final table and partner export by EOD today so I can escalate to finance if needed.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Sophie Marlowe <sophie@techpartner.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NYC Roundtable — lead export and follow-ups

All — closing the loop. Attached is the final attribution breakdown (final-attribution-breakdown.pdf) that combines ACME export, TechPartner export, and our CRM timestamps. High-level outcome:

- Final reconciled leads: 69 credited (3 suppressed duplicates post-match).
- Attribution policy we applied: partner-first-touch for TechPartner-flagged rows (9 leads) + weighted multi-touch for the remainder (weight: on-site 40%, nurture 35%, demo 25%).
- Pipeline impact for INN-4729: $142,500 incremental pipeline recognized to the event (finance-approved provisional).

Next steps:
- Lauren/Finance: please confirm you can accept the attached table as the source of truth for forecasting adjustments.
- Sophie/TechPartner: confirm the 9 matched partner leads — if agreed we'll draft a short MAP clause covering co-sourced credit.
- Ben/Marissa: I'll sync with you tomorrow to update HubSpot tags to preserve on-site first-touch metadata (so future exports don't lose source).

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

--
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
